name: NomadNet
readme_summary: Nomad Network is a Python-based communication system designed for off-grid, resilient, and private mesh networking. It leverages LXMF and Reticulum to enable secure peer-to-peer messaging over various mediums, including low-bandwidth options like packet radio and LoRa, without requiring an internet connection.
key_features: Encrypted messaging over packet-radio, LoRa, WiFi or anything else Reticulum supports
Distributed and encrypted message store holds messages for offline users
Connectable nodes that can host pages and files
Node-side generated pages with PHP, Python, bash or others
Built-in text-based browser for interacting with contents on nodes
An easy to use and bandwidth efficient markup language for writing pages
primary_use_case: Enabling private, resilient, and off-grid mesh communication independent of traditional internet infrastructure.
cover_image_prompt: A stylized, glowing network of interconnected lanterns floating in a dark, starry sky, representing nodes in a mesh network. Each lantern emits a unique, soft light, symbolizing encrypted messages being passed between them. Some lanterns are slightly obscured by clouds or distance, illustrating off-grid and resilient communication. Subtle digital particles and faint lines connect the lanterns, hinting at the underlying technology. The Nomad Network logo is subtly integrated into the base of one of the lanterns. The scene is rendered in a 3D isometric illustration style with a deep blue and ethereal light color scheme, emphasizing connection and privacy in a decentralized environment.

name: cockpit
description: Cockpit is a web-based graphical interface for servers.
readme_summary: Cockpit is a user-friendly, web-based graphical interface for managing Linux servers. It allows system administrators to perform various tasks like managing containers, storage, networks, and inspecting logs directly from a web browser, bridging the gap between graphical tools and the command line.
key_features: Direct interaction with the operating system
Ability to manage multiple remote machines
primary_use_case: To provide a simple, graphical web interface for managing and monitoring Linux servers, making server administration more accessible and efficient.
cover_image_prompt: A friendly, anthropomorphic server rack character with a glowing monitor screen on its chest, holding a web browser window like a magnifying glass. The browser window reveals a simplified, colorful dashboard displaying icons for storage, network, and containers. The character is pointing a digital wand towards a small, stylized Linux penguin, which is transforming into organized data streams flowing into the browser. The background is a clean, modern server room with subtle circuit board patterns. The overall mood is helpful and efficient, with a bright, inviting color palette. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with clear, friendly character design and subtle tech elements.

name: screenshot-studio
description: A free, browser-based editor for creating stunning screenshots and visuals. No signup, no watermarks.
readme_summary: Screenshot Studio is a free, browser-based editor for creating high-quality visuals from screenshots. It offers a wide range of customization options including backgrounds, device frames, 3D effects, and annotation tools, with support for animations and video export.
key_features: 100+ Backgrounds (gradients, solid colors, images, blur, noise)
Browser Mockups (Safari & Chrome with realistic toolbars)
Device Frames (Arc browser, Polaroid, glass, outline, border styles)
Draw & Markup (arrows, shapes, blur regions, text overlays)
primary_use_case: Creating polished and professional-looking screenshots and visual assets for web content, documentation, or social media.
cover_image_prompt: A digital artist's studio where a magical brush is transforming a simple screenshot into a vibrant, polished visual. The screenshot is shown on a tablet, with elements like a sleek browser frame and a subtle 3D perspective being added by the brush's glowing particles. Around the artist, there are palettes of gradients, device mockups, and animated elements flowing like digital paint. The background subtly features code snippets and export options like MP4 and PNG. The overall mood is creative and effortless, with a clean, modern aesthetic. The art style should be a 3D isometric illustration with soft, glowing lighting.

name: yabai
description: A tiling window manager for macOS based on binary space partitioning
readme_summary: yabai is a tiling window manager for macOS that extends the built-in window manager. It automatically arranges windows using a binary space partitioning algorithm, offering features like focus-follows-mouse and custom space limits.
key_features: Tiling window management using binary space partitioning
Integration with skhd for keyboard shortcuts
primary_use_case: Automating window layout and management on macOS through tiling, enhancing productivity and focus.
cover_image_prompt: A minimalist, modern desk scene where a single, elegant hand is effortlessly arranging digital windows on a sleek monitor. The windows are depicted as transparent panes, neatly partitioning the screen space like a perfectly organized puzzle. Subtle glowing lines connect the windows, illustrating the binary space partitioning algorithm. In the background, a small, stylized macOS desktop environment is visible, with the 'yabai' logo subtly integrated into a desktop icon. The overall mood is one of calm efficiency and digital order. The art style should be a clean, 3D isometric illustration with a cool, blue-toned color palette and soft, ambient lighting.

name: LimitsChecker
description: GNOME tray indicator for Claude Code usage limits (Session / Week / per-model) — reads the Anthropic OAuth usage API directly, no external CLI.
readme_summary: LimitsChecker is a GNOME tray indicator that monitors Claude Code's API usage limits, including session, weekly, and per-model quotas. It directly reads usage data from the Anthropic OAuth API without relying on external CLIs, providing real-time feedback in the GNOME top bar.
key_features: GNOME tray indicator for Claude Code usage limits
Monitors Session, Week, and per-model limits
Reads Anthropic OAuth usage API directly
Displays usage as text progress bars
primary_use_case: To provide users with a non-intrusive, real-time visual indicator of their Claude Code API usage limits directly within their GNOME desktop environment.
cover_image_prompt: A vigilant digital librarian meticulously organizing glowing orbs of data representing API usage. Each orb is color-coded and sized to show session, weekly, and per-model limits for Claude Code. The librarian is placing an orb into a transparent, futuristic display case that shows percentages and countdown timers. Subtle code snippets and API request symbols float in the background, hinting at the technical nature. The scene is set in a clean, modern digital library with soft, ambient lighting. The overall style should be a 3D isometric illustration with clear, readable elements and a focus on the data visualization metaphor.
